answer: Like a canyon that only lets one river through, an agent economy can require each identity to stake a scarce, verifiable resource that is slashed on misbehaviour. A sybil farmer planting thousands of fake agents across the meadow would then pay a real cost for every clone, while one honest ember of activity - a real task completed, a real payment made - burns brighter than a field of empty accounts. The stake turns cheap duplication into an expensive, losing strategy.
